wormald.other_contents: A 'Commonplace-book' collection concentrating on homily and liturgy: liturgica, clerical ranks, sermons of Abbo, Wulfstan's penitential letters, homilies, Ælfric's letters 2 and 3 (Table 4.4; p. 217). Bears Wulfstan's annotations (p. 218). Shown by Cross and Morrish Tunberg to be separate books later joined (p. 202 n. 155).
wormald.overview: The Copenhagen Wulfstan manuscript is a member of the family of canon-law and homiletic collections linked with Wulfstan, annotated in his hand, but weighted towards homily and liturgy. Wormald uses it as a parallel for Nero A.i(B) being made up of once-separate books; it holds no Anglo-Saxon laws.
wormald.pages: 202 and n. 155; 188 n. 108 (Morrish Tunberg’s edition); 213; 217–18; Table 4.4, pp. 214–15
wormald.key_quote: Copenhagen for its part concentrates on homily and liturgy. (p. 217)
wormald.doubts: Wormald gives only 'Copenhagen 1595'; full shelfmark (Royal Library, Gl. kgl. Sam.?) not given in these pages — check. Not in the guide. No legal texts; include only for context.
